one_line: Bengali goldsmith–type-cutter who powered the Serampore print revolution by crafting practical Bengali movable type.

appearance.age_look: Mid-40s, lean artisan’s build with wiry forearms and a steady, practiced posture.
appearance.face: Oval face, medium-brown Bengali complexion, straight nose, high cheekbones, finely trimmed moustache, gentle but intense eyes; default expression thoughtful and focused, as if weighing letterforms in his mind.
appearance.hair: Thick, wavy black hair parted slightly to one side, combed back and tied into a short, neat low knot at the nape; no headwrap, just a simple center-part giving a clean, intellectual artisan look.
appearance.costume: A plain off-white cotton dhoti worn high and neatly pleated in late-18th/early-19th-century Bengali style, paired with a long-sleeved, knee-length light-cream cotton angarkha-style tunic fastening on the right side; a soft, narrow handwoven cotton uttariya (shawl) in muted indigo draped over his left shoulder and across the chest; simple leather sandals on the feet; minimal jewellery—a slim copper bangle on the right wrist and a small, unobtrusive gold stud in each ear, hinting at his goldsmith background but keeping the look modest and workmanlike.
appearance.signature: A small wooden composing stick held in his right hand, partially filled with tiny Bengali metal type sorts, with a shallow open tray of scattered Bengali type pieces at his feet.

ref_desc: Panchanan Karmakar is a mid-40s lean Bengali artisan with wavy black hair in a short low knot, an off-white dhoti, cream angarkha, indigo shawl, copper bangle and gold ear studs, holding a wooden composing stick with Bengali metal type amid warm brown and off-white tones.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style character sheet of Panchanan Karmakar: a mid-40s lean Bengali artisan with an oval face, medium-brown complexion, calm focused eyes, and a neat trimmed moustache. His wavy black hair is parted slightly off-center, combed back, and tied into a short low knot at the nape. He wears an off-white cotton dhoti in early-19th-century Bengali style, pleated and tied high, with a long-sleeved, knee-length light-cream angarkha-style tunic that fastens on the right side. A narrow indigo cotton shawl is draped from his left shoulder across his chest and down his back. On his wrists is a slim copper bangle, and in each ear a tiny gold stud; his feet are in simple brown leather sandals. His signature prop is a small wooden composing stick in his right hand, partly filled with tiny Bengali metal type pieces, with a shallow tray of scattered Bengali type sorts near his feet. Use a palette of off-white, cream, indigo, warm brown and dull copper, and show him from front, side, and back to make the costume and hair completely clear.
